question: A company plans to migrate some of its services to the cloud. The company does not want to manage or control the underlying cloud infrastructure. It also wants to maintain control over the deployment of its applications and configuration settings of the application-hosting environment. Which cloud service model meets these requirements?
theory: In the NIST cloud service-model hierarchy, Platform as a Service sits between IaaS and SaaS: the provider fully owns and manages the underlying infrastructure — servers, storage, networking, and OS — while the consumer only manages the applications deployed onto that platform and its configuration settings, exactly matching a company that wants no infrastructure management responsibility but still wants control over how its applications are deployed and configured. IaaS would still require managing the OS and middleware, and SaaS would remove control over the application itself, which is why PaaS is the model that fits both stated requirements. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 5 — Platform as a Service)
